info.title: BYOMailer
info.description:
The BYOMailer API manages the contacts, lists, newsletters, sequences and webhooks of one BYOMailer instance. Each instance has its own URL.

Send a personal API token as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Make the token in Settings, API Tokens. A read-only token gets 403 on each request that changes data. Each request sees only the data of the client of the token user.

List endpoints use cursor pagination. Send `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25) and the `cursor` from `meta.next_cursor` of the previous page.

Errors use the HTTP status code and a JSON body with `message`. A 422 response also has `errors`, with the messages for each field. Each user can send 300 requests a minute (the `API_RATE_LIMIT` setting). Three endpoints have a lower limit. A request over a limit gets 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

An unversioned `/api/<resource>` path answers 308 Permanent Redirect to `/api/v1/<resource>`.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: A contact is one email address of your client, with a name, tags, custom attributes and list memberships. In a create or update request, each body field that is not `email`, `name`, `tags` or `remove_tags` becomes a custom attribute.

tags.name: Lists
tags.description: A list groups contacts. When a list has opt-in, the contact gets a confirmation email and is subscribed only after the confirmation.

tags.name: Topics
tags.description: A topic is a subject inside one list. A contact subscribes to each topic of the list, and can unsubscribe from one topic on the preference page.

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: A tag labels contacts. Use tags to select the audience of a newsletter or a sequence.

tags.name: Newsletters
tags.description: A newsletter is one email to an audience of contacts. Create and edit drafts, schedule a send, pick the winner of an A/B test, and send a test email to yourself.

tags.name: Sequences
tags.description: A sequence is a series of emails. Each enrolled contact gets the steps on a schedule. The API reads sequences, steps and statistics, exports the mails of a step, and changes step filters and content variables.

tags.name: Blocks
tags.description: A block is a reusable piece of HTML content.

tags.name: Email templates
tags.description: An email template is the HTML layout around the content of a newsletter or a sequence step. The API reads templates. Change them in the dashboard.

tags.name: Email identities
tags.description: An email identity is a sender domain or a sender address in the Amazon SES account of your client. The API reads identities. Add them in the dashboard.

tags.name: Email logs
tags.description: An email log is one record of the email activity of your client, for example one send, one bounce or one complaint.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: A project groups newsletters, sequences and automations.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: A webhook endpoint receives a signed `POST` request when an event occurs. Only an admin can manage webhook endpoints. Each delivery has the headers `X-Byomailer-Event`, `X-Byomailer-Delivery`, `X-Byomailer-Timestamp` and `X-Byomailer-Signature`. The signature is `sha256=` and the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the timestamp, a dot and the raw body, with the endpoint secret as the key.

get.description:
Returns the contacts of your client, newest first. Unsubscribed contacts are
left out unless `include_unsubscribed` is true. The filters `lists`, `tags`
and `topics` each match a contact that has one of the given IDs.

parameters.name: lists[]
parameters.description: Return only contacts on one of these list IDs.

parameters.name: tags[]
parameters.description: Return only contacts with one of these tag IDs.

parameters.name: topics[]
parameters.description: Return only contacts subscribed to one of these topic IDs.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Return only contacts whose name or email contains this text.

parameters.name: include_unsubscribed
parameters.description: Also return unsubscribed contacts.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of items on one page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The cursor from `meta.next_cursor` or `meta.prev_cursor` of the previous response.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

prev_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the previous set of items.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

put.description:
Changes the email, the name, the tags or the custom attributes of a contact.
Only the fields in the request change. `tags` adds tags and `remove_tags`
removes tags. Each other body field sets a custom attribute. An update never
changes the subscription. To subscribe a contact again, use the subscribe
endpoint or add the contact to a list.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

patch.description:
Changes the email, the name, the tags or the custom attributes of a contact.
Only the fields in the request change. `tags` adds tags and `remove_tags`
removes tags. Each other body field sets a custom attribute. An update never
changes the subscription. To subscribe a contact again, use the subscribe
endpoint or add the contact to a list.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Adds the contact with this email to the list. If the email is new, the
contact is created and the response is 201. If the contact exists, it is
updated and the response is 200. When the list has opt-in and the contact is
new on the list, the contact gets a confirmation email. A newsletter or a
sequence reaches the contact through this list only after it confirms. Tags
in `tags` are created when they do not exist. A new contact with a
blacklisted email gets 422.
The request never changes the subscription. An unsubscribed contact stays
unsubscribed. To subscribe it again, use the subscribe endpoint.
post.summary: Add a contact to a list

200.description: The contact existed, and the request updated it.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Marks the contact as unsubscribed. The contact then gets no newsletters and
no sequence emails. A second call keeps the first unsubscribe date.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Clears an unsubscribe that an admin or the API made. The contact then gets
newsletters and sequence emails again. A contact that unsubscribed through
an email link gets 422. An address on the suppression list after a
complaint, or on the global suppression list, gets 422. To remove a bounce
suppression of your client, send `remove_suppression` as true. A subscribed
contact does not change.

remove_suppression.description: Remove the bounce suppression of the address. Without it, a suppressed address gets 422.

422.description: The contact unsubscribed through an email link, or the address is on a suppression list that cannot be removed (`contact`). The address has a bounce suppression and `remove_suppression` is not true (`remove_suppression`).

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

delete.description:
Removes the contact from one list. The contact stays in your client and on
its other lists. The removal runs the live list automations of your client.
delete.summary: Remove a contact from a list

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

Returns the newsletters of your client, newest first, with their send
metrics. Filter by status, by project, or by a text in the title or the
subject.

post.description:
Creates a draft newsletter. To schedule it, send `status: live` with
`scheduled_at`, `subject`, `html_content` and a verified
`email_identity_id`. A `scheduled_at` in the past or now queues the send at
once. The send checks the content, the sender and the sending permissions
of your AWS account first. `meta.warnings` lists the compliance warnings of
a scheduled or queued newsletter. They never block the send.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Returns the number of contacts that match the given audience filters.
Nothing is saved. A read-only token can call this endpoint. The limit is 30
requests a minute for each user.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

get.description:
Returns one newsletter with its message, its A/B variant, its filters, its
projects and its send metrics.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

patch.description:
Changes a newsletter with the status `draft` or `scheduled`. Only the fields
in the request change. A newsletter that is sending or sent cannot change
and returns 422, except for a request with only `title` and `project_ids`.
These labels change in any status. A change to a scheduled newsletter must keep a subject and
a body. `status: live` schedules the newsletter, with the same checks as
create. `status: draft` returns a scheduled newsletter to draft and clears
`scheduled_at`. When the send started first, it returns 422 and nothing
changes.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

delete.description:
Deletes a newsletter with the status `draft` or `scheduled`, with its
messages. Other statuses return 422. When the send of a scheduled
newsletter started first, it returns 422 and nothing changes.

422.description: The newsletter is sending or sent, or its send started first (`status`).

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

get.description:
A named link (`data-bm-link` attribute) groups by its name. Any other link
groups by its URL without the `utm_*` parameters and the fragment. Use the
`key` of a link to list its contacts. The click rate is unique contacts
divided by delivered mails, times 100. Clicks can include link scanners,
for example Microsoft Safe Links.
get.summary: List the links of a newsletter with their clicks

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

get.description:
Send the `key` of a link from the link list in the `link` parameter. Each
contact shows its number of clicks on that link and the time of the first
click. The list uses cursor pagination.
get.summary: List the contacts who clicked one link of a newsletter

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: A link key from the link list, for example `name:black-friday` or `url:https://example.com/sale`.

path.description: Base path for paginator generated URLs.

per_page.description: Number of items shown per page.

next_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the next set of items.

prev_cursor.description: The "cursor" that points to the previous set of items.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Sends the newsletter to the email address of the token user, through the SES
account of your client. The newsletter needs a verified email identity. The
limit is 5 requests a minute for each user.

422.description: The newsletter has no sender (`email_identity_id`), or SES did not accept the email (`send`).

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

post.description:
Stores variant `a` or `b` as the winner of an A/B test. The newsletter must
have the status `ab_testing`. Each half of the audience already got one
variant, so BYOMailer sends no more email. The newsletter gets the status
`sent`, and the `newsletter.sent` webhook event fires one time.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

get.description:
Returns the `{{ variables }}` that the content of the newsletter uses, and
the saved default of each one. A default fills a variable when the contact
has no value for it.
get.summary: Get the content variables of a newsletter

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

patch.description:
Replaces the content variable defaults of a newsletter with the status
`draft` or `scheduled`. The object replaces all saved defaults. A default
can name a variable that the content does not use yet. Each variable
that the content uses and the object leaves out gets an empty default.
patch.summary: Replace the content variables of a newsletter

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before you send the request again.

AbVariant.title: AbVariant
